[...] The HFPS reaches an energy of -0.76413 which is somewhat higher then the -0.76486(2) of our symmetry optimization with 32 determinants. Additionally, our result can be further projected at essentially no cost to the fully symmetric state to reach an energy of -0.76560(1) [...] The optimization of our 32 determinant MLP-NNBF is faster by approximately a factor of 2 compared with the HFPS. || Sec. II.B: All optimizations reported in this paper were performed using H100 GPUs on GH200 superchips. Most optimizations were performed using a single H100 GPU, but longer optimizations were parallelized across 4 GPUs. GPU times are reported as cumulative GPU usage (e.g. parallelized times are 4 times the wall clock time). All optimization times include the cumulative cost of optimization for a given point which includes (where specified) optimizing smaller ansatz first. || Appendix B: Unless otherwise specified, the total number of markov chains is fixed at N_s = 1024 and the learning rate is fixed at 3 x 10^-4. We first train the single particle orbitals without backflow for 10^5 VMC iterations. [...] The training for the data in Fig. A1 took 3 x 10^6 VMC iterations, followed by 5 x 10^5 VMC iterations with an exponential decay learning rate schedule tuning the learning rate to 10^-7. The training for the model with 4 symmetries took approximately 8 x 10^5 VMC iterations, while the training for the model with 32 symmetries took approximately 5 x 10^5 VMC iterations. || Sec. II.A: Our MLP is fully connected with two hidden layers each followed by a layer normalization and relu activation. || Sec. II.A: u(n) is the output, an N\times L matrix, of an MLP with input n [...] Here both spin sectors are combined into a single matrix (e.g. N is the sum of the spin up and down electrons and L is twice the number of physical sites) [...] Our MLP is fully connected with two hidden layers each followed by a layer normalization and relu activation. The input layer is set by |n> = |n_0, n_1, ..., n_L> where n_i \in {-1,1} denotes an empty or occupied spin orbital. The last output layer contains a bias but no non-linear function; this bias can be interpreted as a fixed mean-field solution onto which the neural network provides additive configuration-dependent backflow corrections. || Sec. III: A fixed depth multi-layer MLP-NNBF scales as O(n_o n_h + n_h^2 + \alpha n_h n_o^2 + (\alpha n_o)^3) per step where n_o is the number of orbitals and \alpha is the filling fraction.
